_description: Fallbacks applied when the env is constructed with a config dict that omits a key - a bare continuousDoubleAuctionEnv({}), a test fixture, or an RLlib env_config that only sets a few keys. Read through config_loader.env_default; the env holds no literal for any of them.
_note: These are STANDALONE defaults and deliberately differ from the training defaults in train_config.json: a bare env is small (num_of_agents 5, max_step 64) and renders, a training env is large and silent. Keys here use the env-side spelling: num_of_agents, not the TrainConfig field name num_agents. TrainConfig.env_config always supplies every key below, so a training run never reaches these.
_note_init_cash: init_cash must be > 0. Trader._order_approved refuses on nav <= 0 before it inspects anything else, so a bare env built with init_cash 0 - as this file shipped until now - starts every trader bankrupt: no order is ever placed, Done_Helper.set_done puts every agent in done_set on the first pass, and terminateds['__all__'] is True after a single step(), so max_step is unreachable. It matches cli_defaults.json and train_config.json at 1,000,000 so all three agree. test_bare_env_is_tradable pins it.

environment._note_mark_price_source: mark_price_source picks the price every account is marked at. 'mid' is the L1 midpoint, falling back to the one-sided quote and then to the last tape print; 'last' is the last tape print alone, which is what this used to do unconditionally. It is a key rather than a constant because the change moves NAV dynamics. Marking off the last print is what made self-matching profitable (finding S2-5): one self-traded contract at a chosen price re-marked the whole market, including the self-trader's own reward - measured at 1,000 NAV moved by a single 1-lot print. Self-match prevention now stops the print from happening, and marking to mid removes the payoff even if some other path ever produces one.
environment._note_episode_length: episode_length_mode picks how long an episode runs. 'fixed': every episode is truncated at max_step. 'random': each reset draws the horizon uniformly from [max_step_min, max_step_max] (inclusive) with the env's seeded generator, so a policy cannot learn the exact end of the game - the end-game is where a known horizon lets an agent dump inventory for free - and the drawn value is reported as episode_horizon in the reset infos. time_left is then measured against max_step_max, the latest possible end, not against the draw: showing the draw would hand the horizon back. max_step is ignored in 'random' mode except as TrainConfig's default for the two bounds. Termination on bankruptcy is unchanged in both modes.
environment._note_is_render: is_render was true here, so every bare continuousDoubleAuctionEnv({}) built a tabulate table of the whole book, the tape and every account on every step - for a logger that drops it unless it is at DEBUG (doc/15 S4-7). false since 2026-09-18; CDA_rand --render and a DEBUG cda_log_level are the two ways to ask for it, and both still work.
environment._note_book_mode: book_mode picks how the public book is laid out in each observation snapshot (doc/15 S3-15). 'grid': two rows of sqrt(V / limit_max_size) sizes, bids and asks, over a window of 2 * k_rows + 1 tick offsets centred on the reference price R (the midpoint of a two-sided book, else the last trade, snapped to the tick); cell c is the price R + (c - k_rows) * tick, so the same cell means the same distance on every step and in every frame of the stack, and the action's price code j quotes exactly j ticks from R on the passive side. 'levels': the k_rows best occupied prices per side with their prices, sizes and occupancy (six rows), the representation before 2026-09-18, kept so the two can be compared with train.compare. Measured under random play in levels mode, the best level sat 3.8 +- 2.5 ticks from R and its price changed on 35-54% of steps, and the same price code landed anywhere from 0 to 20 ticks out; a +-10-tick window covers 73% (shipped) to 81% (stress) of resting volume, k_rows widens it. Recorded in the checkpoint's layout stamp.
environment._note_action_mask: action_mask: when true (the default) the last nine entries of each agent's private observation block say which of the nine action categories is POSSIBLE for that agent this step, and the PPO modules and the random baselines refuse the others: modify or cancel on a side where the agent has nothing resting (the 'unmatched' dead action, 27-30% of random agent-steps before this), and a market or limit order the cash check would refuse at the reference price for the minimum size (the 'rejected' dead action). Pass is always possible. What is merely unwise - cancelling a good quote - is left to the policy to learn. When false the env emits all ones, so the layout is the same and train.compare --set action_mask=false is the unmasked baseline (doc/16 section 16.25).
environment._note_matching_rule: matching_rule picks how the quantity reaching one price level is split among the orders resting there (doc/06 section 8). 'fifo' is price-time priority - the oldest order fills first - the default and what a continuous double auction runs. 'pro_rata' splits it in proportion to resting size, largest-remainder rounded to whole contracts with the residue in time order, the rule some futures markets use; it rewards size over speed, and a policy that learns it will post larger orders to win allocation. Kept pluggable so the regimes can be compared under identical seeds with train.compare --set matching_rule=pro_rata.
environment._note_step_clearing: step_clearing picks what happens when several agents' orders cross within the same step, i.e. the same instant (doc/06 section 8). 'sequential' (default): the step's actions are shuffled and each order is matched on arrival, so a crossing pair's price and who fills against resting liquidity depend on where the shuffle put them - the continuous double auction's random tie-break. 'batch': the step's new market and limit orders (and a modify's re-entered quote) are queued and cleared together against the resting book at ONE uniform price - the volume-maximising price, then the smallest imbalance, then the one closest to the reference - with resting orders keeping time priority and the marginal level rationed under matching_rule; leftover limits rest, leftover markets lapse. Order-management actions (cancel) apply immediately in both. Measured under random play: the first agent in the shuffle filled 1.x times as often as the last under sequential clearing and equally often under batch (doc/16 section 16.26).
environment._note_liquidation: liquidation picks what happens when a trader's equity runs out (doc/04 section 8). 'gradual_adl' is 'market_adl' spread over up to liquidation_horizon steps (see below). 'market_adl' (default): at the end of every step a live trader with NAV <= maintenance_margin x |net_position| x mark is closed out - its resting orders are cancelled, an immediate-or-cancel order for the whole position goes to the book limited to the trader's bankruptcy price (the worst price at which its NAV stays >= 0), and whatever the book cannot absorb inside that band is transferred at the mark to the live traders on the opposite side, pro rata to their positions (auto-deleveraging). The trader is then flat; it keeps trading if NAV > 0 and is terminated if NAV <= 0. 'off': the behaviour before 2026-09-19 - no margin, and a trader terminated at NAV <= 0 keeps its position, which is marked to the end of the episode: measured in CDA_train.ipynb, a bankrupt short went on to -1.9M while the agents on the other side collected it from a counterparty that could not act.
environment._note_maintenance_margin: maintenance_margin is the equity a position must keep as a fraction of its value at the mark. Positions here are fully paid - the cash check escrows 100% of an opening order - so a long's equity never falls below its value and only shorts can breach: an all-in short breaches when the price has risen (1 - m) / (1 + m) above its entry, 54% at 0.3, where NAV <= 0 needed 100%. 0.3 is the maintenance US brokers apply to short stock (FINRA Rule 4210). 0 liquidates at bankruptcy, NAV <= 0. Must be in [0, 1).
environment._note_liquidation_horizon: liquidation_horizon is used by liquidation 'gradual_adl' only: the most steps a close-out may take. On breach the account is frozen (every order refused, so the action mask shows only pass), and each step an immediate-or-cancel order for ceil(remaining / steps_left) goes to the book inside the bankruptcy band recomputed from that step's NAV and mark; what the book does not take rolls into later slices, and on the last step ADL closes the rest. If NAV reaches 0 meanwhile, the remainder is closed at once. 1 is 'market_adl'. Must be >= 1.
environment._note_position_scale: position_scale divides net_position before the tanh in the private observation block. Deliberately not limit_max_size, which is what it used to be: that is a sizing parameter - it scales the mean of the Gaussian _set_size draws from and bounds nothing - while inventory accumulates over many fills. Measured over 7,200 agent-steps of random play at default config, |net_position| has a median of 372, a p90 of 1,195, a p95 of 1,485 and a maximum of 1,831, so limit_max_size of 1,000 put 13.2% of agent-steps into tanh saturation. 1500 is that p95, which keeps the feature in its responsive range across the observed distribution (finding S2-2).
environment._note_reward_coefficients: Reward coefficients. Every one multiplies a quantity already expressed as a FRACTION OF STARTING NAV (reward_helper.set_reward divides by trader.acc.init_nav), so 1e-05 is one basis point of initial capital. Measured over 8,000 random-agent steps: a step that moves NAV at all moves it by a median 1.9e-03 of starting capital (p90 7.3e-03), and 37% of steps move it at all. The micro-penalties are set at ~0.5-1% of that median move - a nudge on order placement, not a tax that dominates the P&L, which is what finding S2-3 was about when they were 0.1 and 0.05 against raw dollar NAV.
environment._note_drawdown_penalty: drawdown_penalty multiplies the SIGNED CHANGE in drawdown, not the level. The level was charged on all 4,096 steps of an episode, so one early loss taxed every later step even from an idle agent (finding S2-1). Signed rather than clipped at zero: clipping would charge nav_term twice on every losing step and refund nothing on recovery, which is an asymmetric loss multiplier by another name. Signed, the charges telescope to -drawdown_penalty * final_drawdown over an episode, so a round trip is free and the term cannot be farmed.
environment._note_loss_multiplier: loss_multiplier MUST be 1.0 to keep the game zero-sum. Total NAV is conserved exactly, so sum(nav_change) == 0 across agents; any value above 1 makes sum(reward) < 0, which makes passing dominant for every agent and collapses the market (finding S1-3, measured: all-pass scored exactly 0.0 while random trading scored -591,027). It shipped at 1.5.
environment._note_dead_action_penalty: dead_action_penalty multiplies num_unmatched_step - modify/cancel actions this step that named no resting order (doc/15 S3-24 phase 3). Zero by default, deliberately: any positive value makes sum(reward) < 0 across agents, which is the negative-sum bias finding S1-3 removed, so turning it on is a measured decision, not a default. The miss is already visible to the policy through the unmatched_last_step observation field, which costs nothing.
